beats.summary: Andy and Dwight introduce a new accountability program called the 'accountability booster' that tracks office mistakes and triggers consequences.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: The accountability booster. It registers every time a mistake has been made in the office.
Andy: If we as a group make five mistakes in a day, something bad happens like we block Minesweeper.

beats.summary: Office workers express concern and resistance to the accountability booster, fearing it is a doomsday device and that it will ruin their lives.

evidence.snippet: Kelly: Um, no we're not and you are a psycho who is ruining our lives.
Ryan: We can't do this Dwight.

beats.summary: The accountability booster registers mistakes during the workday, creating tension and prompting employees to be extra careful.

evidence.snippet: Dwight (alert goes off): Oh, there's one mistake.
Erin: Now we only have four strikes left until a home run.

beats.summary: Gabe makes humorous remarks about Val and the support belt, including a cow-milking gesture and a Michelin man cummerbund joke.

evidence.snippet: Gabe: I get the sense that Val enjoys a good putdown. ConsidEring that's the only thing I know about her. I will be milking that hard.
Gabe: The Michelin man called, he wants his cummerbund back.

beats.summary: Jim and Dwight discuss the accountability booster, with Jim questioning its potential negative consequences and Dwight expressing confidence it will work.

evidence.snippet: Jim: If this bad idea goes off and we all lose our jobs. Are you going to feel good about that?
Dwight: I haven't even considered it. That's how sure I am that this accountability booster is going to work.

beats.summary: Darryl and Gabe interact about reading a packet and getting coffee, with Gabe requesting a decaf frappuccino and Darryl teasing him.

evidence.snippet: Darryl: Actually, Val, why don't you come with? I'll need the extra hands to carry them back.
